### 5.3 Training and Inference Details
Our evaluation metrics, detailed in Tables 1 and 2 and following [5], include both accuracy and ROC-AUC. Accuracy measures the proportion of correctly classified instances among the total instances, providing a straightforward metric for model performance. The ROC-AUC (Receiver Operating Characteristic - Area Under the Curve) score, representing the degree of separability, is particularly valuable for assessing performance on imbalanced datasets, such as in link prediction tasks with a substantial class imbalance between positive and negative edges. Summarizing the results across these diverse tasks, tables 3 , 4,

Fig. 2: Performance After Pruning: The plots show GCN, GAT, and Graph-
SAGE performance on OGBN-ARXIV (node classification), OGBL-COLLAB
(link prediction), and OGBG-MOHLIV (graph classification) at a pruning weight
fraction of 0.3. GLTs are marked by red $(\star)$ and green $(\star)$ stars, indicating com-
parable performance despite sparsity, while dashed lines represent pre-pruning
baselines. The plot sections correspond to node classification (top), link predic-
tion (middle), and graph classification (bottom).

related_claims.content: Magnitude-based iterative pruning identifies subnetworks that match baseline performance at sparsity levels down to approximately 1–20% of the original parameter count across multiple architectures and tasks.

Magnitude-based iterative pruning identifies subnetworks that match baseline performance at sparsity levels down to approximately 1–20% of the original parameter count across the architectures QGCN, QGAT, and QSAGE and tasks.
QMPNN variants scale to large graph datasets and maintain performance comparable to real-valued GNNs while using fewer parameters.

Across all tasks and datasets evaluated, quaternion variants of standard GNN architectures frequently perform within a small margin of the corresponding real models and sometimes exceed their performance while consistently having approximately one-fourth the trainable parameter count of the corresponding real models.

claims.R: comparable to pre-pruning baselines despite sparsity
claims.S: In Figure 2, for GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE at a pruning weight fraction of 0.3 on OGBN-ARXIV (node classification), OGBL-COLLAB (link prediction), and OGBG-MOHLIV (graph classification)

equivalent_claims.content: In Figure 2, performance on OGBN-ARXIV, OGBL-COLLAB, and OGBG-MOHLIV is comparable to the dashed pre-pruning baselines for the red/green-starred GLTs of GCN, GAT, and GraphSAGE after pruning to a weight fraction of 0.3, despite sparsity.
